A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same lattice interpretation of quantization and GPTQ–Babai equivalence. All nine pages of each are readable, including equations, diagrams, references, and v2's new Appendices A–B; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, geometric explanations, and theoretical guarantees, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical, including its appendices. Section 3 explicitly leaves experimental evaluation for future work; the mentioned Qronos experiments are attributed to Zhang et al.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds BABAI-CHOLESKY, computing residuals with the n-by-n triangular factor L and replacing data-space inner products with coordinate division. The original GPTQ/Babai procedures remain unchanged. Section 3 also formalizes the previously suggested basis-reduction wrapper.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or test scenarios. The single-unit and multilayer quantization problems remain theoretical discussions.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. GPTQ and Babai remain subjects of an equivalence proof, rather than evaluated competing methods.

E3.justification: Neither version supplies an experimental evaluation protocol. Appendix A's newly stated block size B=infinity explains the theoretical GPTQ formulation, rather than changing an evaluated configuration.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The added algorithmic arguments are theoretical.

E5.justification: Both versions lack repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests.

E6.justification: No original measured results or experimental result entries are added, removed, or revised. The changed mathematical bounds belong to T1; v2's mention of Qronos improvements cites another work's experiments.

T1.justification: Theorem A/2.1 replaces 'invertible' with the appropriate full-column-rank condition. Theorem 3.1 adds a factor of 1/4 to the squared-error bound, and Theorem 3.2 changes sqrt(n−1) to sqrt(n+1). V2 also states Gram-matrix invariance. The central equivalence proof is retained, with its existing shift-invariance argument made more explicit.

C1.justification: The central CVP interpretation and GPTQ–Babai equivalence claims remain unchanged. Section 3 removes numerical improvements as a stated consequence and narrows basis-reduction benefits from improvements 'in theory and in practice' to theoretical benefits with experimental evaluation deferred.

C2.justification: V2 replaces numerical-stability advocacy with memory/computation considerations and adds warnings about large coefficients, clipping, and calibration overfitting under insufficient regularization. Its new Section 2 mechanism summary is misleading: applying X+ to Babai's residual and dropping coordinates retains the original remaining weights, rather than generally producing GPTQ's updated weights.

D1.justification: Appendix A explicitly documents the unblocked GPTQ setting B=infinity and correspondence with the original algorithms. Appendix B supplies reverse-Cholesky computation details, while Section 3 specifies basis-change and output-reconstruction steps. No implementation release, hardware information, or empirical hyperparameters are added.

R1.justification: The same eight cited works and the independent, shorter-proof positioning relative to Chen et al. are retained. GPTQ/OPTQ and the updated Chen and Qronos conference references correspond to works already cited in v1; their bibliographic updates do not establish new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main three-section narrative and much of its prose remain intact. V2 removes the contents list, adds Appendices A–B, and expands selected algorithm, proof, and consequences explanations, alongside local wording and author/header edits.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into the ICLR layout, changing title/abstract treatment, margins, headings, equation numbering, and algorithm displays throughout. V1's introductory lattice sketch is removed; its Figures 2–4 survive as v2 Figures 1–3 with resized placement. Additional pseudocode blocks are displayed.

improvement.justification: V2 fixes the erroneous sqrt(n−1) bound in Theorem 3.2, documents efficient computation, and qualifies v1's practical basis-reduction claims with concrete limitations. Its new X+-then-truncation summary introduces a misleading explanation, but the retained recursive proof does not depend on that shortcut. The corrections and practical qualifications provide a limited net improvement.
